# Third-party test data

Files in this directory that did not originate here, with the terms they are
provided under. Keep the notices below with any copy of these files.

Two layers matter for each file and are recorded separately: the terms under
which it was **obtained**, and who created the **model** it contains. A project
can only license what it owns, so a permissive repository holding someone else's
data does not by itself settle the second layer.

Every file in this directory is covered below. Nothing may be added to this
directory until its entry here is written.

---

## Files obtained from pglib-opf (CC BY 4.0)

`pglib_opf_case5_pjm.m`, `pglib_opf_case14_ieee.m` and `pglib_opf_case118_ieee.m`
are byte-for-byte copies from <https://github.com/power-grid-lib/pglib-opf>
(v23.07). That repository's `LICENSE` separates the two layers explicitly, and
is quoted here in full on the point that matters:

```
Data License:

Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license
http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

See data files for specific copyright holders and attribution details.
```

(The repository's *software* is MIT; the case files are data, and are the CC BY
4.0 layer.) Each file names its own copyright holder in its header, and those
headers are the attribution CC BY 4.0 requires. **Do not strip them.**

- `pglib_opf_case14_ieee.m` and `pglib_opf_case118_ieee.m`:
  `Copyright (c) 1999 by Richard D. Christie, University of Washington
  Electrical Engineering`, converted from the IEEE Common Data Format files at
  <http://www.ee.washington.edu/research/pstca/>.
- `pglib_opf_case5_pjm.m`: `Copyright (c) 2010 by The Institute of Electrical
  and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)`, based on F. Li and R. Bo, "Small Test
  Systems for Power System Economic Studies", IEEE PES General Meeting 2010.
  The header asks that M. E. Brennan (me.brennan@ieee.org) be contacted about
  further reuse.

### ieee14.raw and ieee118.raw — derived from the above

These two are **not** third-party files. They are written by this package's own
`RawWriter` from `pglib_opf_case14_ieee.m` and `pglib_opf_case118_ieee.m`, and
are regenerated by re-running that conversion. CC BY 4.0 requires that
modifications be indicated, so, precisely:

- The format was changed from MATPOWER `.m` to PSS/E RAW v33.
- Only what the psforge data model carries survives the conversion. Generator
  cost curves, per-branch ratings and bus voltage limits present in the source
  are not written to RAW.
- No value was added, inferred or corrected. In particular the operating point
  is pglib's, unchanged: bus voltages are flat (1.0 pu, 0 degrees) and
  generation does not cover load, because the pglib cases are OPF *inputs*, not
  solved power flows.
- `ieee14.raw` therefore declares `BASKV = 1.0` on every bus: pglib's 14-bus
  file normalises base voltages away. That is what the source says, and it was
  not filled in from elsewhere. pglib's 118-bus file does carry base voltages
  (138 / 161 / 345 kV), so `ieee118.raw` has them.
- Bus names are absent for the same reason: pglib's files carry none.

`ieee14.psfg.json` is generated from `ieee14.raw` and inherits all of the above.

## 39bus.raw — New England 39-bus system (PSS/E RAW v34)

- **Obtained from**: <https://github.com/NatLabRockies/ParaEMT_public>,
  `models/39bus_psse/39bus.raw`, byte-for-byte unmodified.
- **Terms**: BSD 3-Clause (`LICENSE.md` of that repository), reproduced below.
  The repository states no exception for its data files.
- **Model credit**: the file's own header reads
  `NEW ENGLAND TEST SYSTEM, 39 BUSES, 9 GENERATORS / CREATED BY PABLO LEDESMA
  PABLOLE@ING.UC3M.ES` (Universidad Carlos III de Madrid). That header is the
  attribution and must not be stripped.
- **Why it is here**: it is the only PSS/E **v34** file in this directory, and it
  was written by PSS/E itself (`PSS(R)E-34.8 FRI, DEC 09 2022`). Tests that read
  only files psforge wrote cannot show that psforge reads what other tools
  produce. Its `@!` header comments also document the real field order of each
  record, which is what the generator record's `RMPCT` position was checked
  against.

## ACTIVSg2000.raw — synthetic 2000-bus model of the Texas grid (PSS/E RAW v33)

- **Obtained from**: Texas A&M University Electric Grid Test Case Repository,
  <https://electricgrids.engr.tamu.edu/electric-grid-test-cases/activsg2000/>.
- **Terms**, quoted from that page: "This power system dataset is synthetic and
  does not represent any actual grid. It is provided by Texas A&M University
  researchers free for commercial or non-commercial use." The repository asks
  users to cite the corresponding papers.
- **Citation requested**: the papers listed on the repository's references page —
  reference [1] for the base case, [4] for economic data, [5] for dynamics.
- **Origin**: developed with support of the U.S. DOE ARPA-E GRID DATA program.
  The file's own second line states it contains no CEII.
- **Why it is here**: the only fixture large enough to exercise eight areas, ten
  voltage levels, 3206 branches and out-of-service generators. See
  `test_large_case.py`.

## Files generated here

`ieee14_contingencies.psfg.json` is written for this test suite and contains no
third-party data. It references `ieee14.psfg.json` as its base case.

## Removed, and why — do not restore

Three files were removed in the 0.10.0 cycle because their provenance could not
be established. Do not add them back, under any name.

| File | Obtained from | Problem |
|------|---------------|---------|
| `ieee14.raw` (old) | `ITI/models` | No `LICENSE` file in that repository. The file's second line is `08/19/93 UW ARCHIVE` — the data is the University of Washington's, which that repository redistributes without holding. Replaced by the pglib-derived file above. |
| `ieee118_powsybl.raw` | `powsybl/powsybl-distribution` | Same pattern: no `LICENSE` file in the repository (only an MPL-2.0 badge in its README), and the file's second line is `08/25/93 UW ARCHIVE`. Replaced by `ieee118.raw`. |
| `ieee9.raw` | `todstewart1001/PSSE-24-Hour-Load-Dispatch-IEEE-9-Bus-System-` | No `LICENSE` file. No replacement was available: pglib has no 9-bus case, and MATPOWER's `LICENSE` excludes its case files from its BSD grant, so `case9.m` could not be used either. The v34 coverage it provided is carried by `39bus.raw`. |
